content.title: About
content.content: Pork steak coated with breadcrumbs is a cut of pork that has been breaded with a mixture of crumbs, spices and sometimes egg, then fried. The coating creates a crunchy exterior while the interior stays juicy and tender.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The coating often contains a blend of breadcrumbs, herbs and spices, giving the dish a fragrant flavor.
Breaded pork steak is popular in fast‑food and home cooking, especially when served with barbecue or mustard sauces.
Traditionally the crumbs are made from white bread, but whole‑grain or gluten‑free alternatives can be used.
When fried correctly, the crust remains crisp even after a short rest in sauce.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Pork provides high‑quality complete protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: It supplies thiamine, niacin, B6 and B12, which support energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Source of zinc and iron
items.content: These minerals are important for immune health, blood formation and oxygen transport.

items.title: Contains healthy fats
items.content: Lean portions of pork contain monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fats that can support heart health when eaten in moderation.

items.title: Promotes satiety
items.content: High protein and moderate fat content help keep you feeling full longer.

items.title: Processing and additives
items.content: Breaded products may contain salt, trans‑fats and preservatives; people with high blood pressure or sensitivities should choose additive‑free versions.

items.title: Calorie density
items.content: A coated steak is more calorie‑dense than a lean, unbreaded cut.

items.title: Risk of overeating
items.content: The crunchy crust can encourage rapid eating, leading to excess intake.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Traditional breadcrumbs contain wheat; those with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity need a gluten‑free coating.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: For best results, pan‑fry the coated steak over medium heat until golden, then finish in a 180 °C oven for 10‑15 minutes. Serve with roasted vegetables, mashed potatoes or a fresh salad. Complement with sauces such as barbecue, mustard or creamy dill.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked steak in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 2‑3 days. For longer storage, freeze in a zip‑lock bag at –18 °C, where it remains good for 2‑3 months. Reheat thoroughly before serving.
